title: Kogoro's Class Reunion Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. Two-parter: part 1 (ep027) sets up the apparent suicide and the false ~3:00 PM time of death; part 2 (ep028) reveals the real ~6:30 PM murder, timed to the fireworks show, and the exercise-accelerated-rigor-mortis trick (explicitly compared in-dialogue to the legend of the warrior Benkei dying on his feet). Honest gap: this episode's transcript gives no stated motive or threat from Jun Omura, Yukio Ayashiro, or Noriko Ayashiro against Yumi -- the only red-herring material the source supports is Omura's own suspicious, initially-disbelieved testimony (he genuinely saw Yumi alive well after her presumed death), which is captured as a red-herring implicates edge rather than a fabricated has_motive_against edge. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: No burn marks or gunshot residue around the entry wound, even though a contact or near-contact self-inflicted shot to the head should leave them from the hot gas that accompanies the bullet -- rules out suicide.

The victim's right hand, holding the gun, has its index finger sticking out stiffly instead of on the trigger -- matching the exact shakehand grip she's shown using in an old team photo, revealing her hand had already frozen mid-ping-pong-game rather than around the trigger.

Rigor mortis normally takes hours to progress as far as it had by the time the body was examined, but sudden death immediately after intense physical exertion is medically documented to accelerate it drastically (the same principle behind the legend of the warrior Benkei dying on his feet) -- meaning the body's apparent ~7-hours-dead state is consistent with a death much later than 3:00 PM if the victim had just been made to exert herself.

The yukata on the body is noticeably larger than the one Yumi was seen wearing earlier, and she has no undergarments on underneath it -- someone redressed the body after death, most likely to hide sweat that would have given away recent physical exertion.

Omura insists he saw Yumi glaring down from an upstairs window shortly after 5:00 PM -- well after her presumed 3:00 PM death -- and is initially disbelieved or suspected of hiding something himself, but the sighting turns out to be genuine and is the key to recovering the real ~6:30 PM time of death.

Nakamichi identified Yumi as dead the instant he saw her covered in blood, without ever touching the body to check for a pulse, and called the police rather than an ambulance -- behavior only explainable if he already knew for certain she was dead.
